{{RequisiteWeapon|Ingredient For = {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}}} {{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Evoking the design of ancient bows, the high impact Cernos is perfect for hunting down highly shielded enemies.}} The '''Cernos''' is a {{Faction|Tenno}} Bow, and the first one available to new players that deals mainly {{D|Impact}} damage over another type. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|10,500}}. It is also a [[weapon crafting ingredient]] for {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}. {{Checklist|nocategory=true| * {{Weapon|Cernos}} → {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}} * {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}} → {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}} (extra Cernos is needed if player wants to keep one copy of Mutalist Cernos) }} ==Characteristics== This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. {{Advantages|class=Bow|}} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow|}} {{WeaponComparison|Cernos Prime}} {{WeaponComparison|Rakta Cernos|header=n}} ==Acquisition== The Cernos's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Tips== *Despite what its description says, the Cernos is most effective against {{Faction|Grineer}} , which are primarily ''armored,'' not shielded. Its damage spread being weighted primarily towards Impact means the majority of the weapon's damage will inherit the element's [[Faction Damage Bonus]] against them, dealing solid damage even through their armor. **Impact's status effect of reducing the target's [[Mercy]] threshold also logically counteracts their armor, allowing heavy enemies to be executed even with most of their health remaining, once their [[Overguard]] is broken, after suffering enough Impact procs. ***While the Cernos has a low base status chance relative to its rate of fire and projectile count, this can easily be fixed with modding. {{M|Rifle Aptitude}} will bring it up to a respectable 34%, which can be rolled multiple times per shot by adding multishot mods, such as {{M|Split Chamber}}. **Adding Corrosive damage to the Cernos is a good idea, enhancing how much damage it can do to Grineer enemies even further. **The Cernos is also strong against enemies of the {{Faction|Scaldra}} and {{Faction|Anarchs}} factions, though by the time the player is able to fight these enemies, they will likely have replaced the Cernos with a superior weapon, such as one of its upgraded counterparts. *The Cernos is very statistically similar to the {{Weapon|Paris}} and {{Weapon|Dread}}, two other Bows that become available by the time it is. The three primarily vary in which physical element they are most weighted towards, though the Dread will generally be the last of the three a new player obtains unless they're especially lucky. Thus, if the player has used either of the other two Bows, they will likely know how to use the Cernos. *With a maxed {{M|Critical Delay}} mod, the Cernos' [[critical chance]] will increase to 103.3%. This breaks the 100% critical chance threshold, guaranteeing every hit will be a critical hit and giving the weapon a very small chance to "orange crit", whereupon a critical hit will have its critical multiplier doubled. **Using a maxed Critical Delay however will also drastically reduce the Cernos's [[fire rate]], due to mods that modify this stat having their effect doubled on Bows, making each Cernos arrow take a long time to draw back. This can be countered with the usage of a fire rate mod, such as {{M|Speed Trigger}}. ***Even with only {{M|Point Strike}}, the Cernos will reach 90% critical chance, causing its hits to be critical far more often than they aren't. **If this modding avenue is chosen, adding as many critical damage mods to the Cernos as possible is advised, as they will apply on every hit for a very large damage increase. **At the Mastery Rank the Cernos is unlocked, the Dread and {{Weapon|Cinta}} are also capable of exceeding 100% critical chance. Of the three, the Cernos is generally the easiest to obtain. ==Trivia== *The name "Cernos" means "horn" in Gaulish. *Despite being more effective against the highly-armored {{Faction|Grineer}}, the Cernos's description says it's effective against "highly shielded enemies", implying it's effective against the Corpus instead, who are instead vulnerable to {{D|Puncture}} damage. This is an artifact from before [[Update 36|Update 36.0]], where [[Damage 2.0|Damage 2.0's]] health types system instead made Impact damage stronger against [[Shield|energy shielding]] regardless of faction, while Puncture was stronger against most forms of armor. After the update, which replaced this system with [[Damage 3.0|Damage 3.0's]] faction multipliers and swapped the Corpus and Grineer's vulnerabilities, the Cernos's description was not updated to compensate, and still has not been as of [[Update 41: The Old Peace#Hotfix 41.1.2|Hotfix 41.1.2]] (2-17-2026). *Being an Impact oriented bow, the Cernos uses arrows with a mace-like head, with a larger impact area. This spreads the kinetic energy of the arrows across a wider area, creating a blunt impact, hence its damage distribution. **Despite this, the Cernos's arrows can still pin enemies they kill to walls. Judging by the hole in the middle of the head, it's possible the arrows are hollow to house a spring-loaded punch system that fires a spike upon impact, though no such animation exists in-game if [[Captura]] mode's camera is used to watch the arrows mid-flight. **The [[Prisma Arrows|Prisma Arrows skin]] highly resembles the Cernos's arrows, and can be equipped to any Bow-type weapon. *As of {{ver|30.3}}, the Cernos has the most variations of all weapons, having a total of 5 weapons in its family; the normal {{Weapon|Cernos}}, {{Weapon|Rakta Cernos}}, {{Weapon|Cernos Prime}}, {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}, and {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}}. **The Cernos is the first weapon to have two upgraded forms, with both its Mutalist and Proboscics variants requiring the other form respectively in order to be built. **The Cernos is also one of the few weapons to have variants that are considered separate weapons for the sake of mechanics like Riven mods, rather than direct variants, that aren't simply an akimbo version of the weapon. The {{Weapon|Quanta}} is another. ==Media== Warframe0150.jpg|Cernos in the Codex. Cernos Arsenal.png|Cernos as shown in the Arsenal Cernos Arrow quiver.png|Cernos Arrow Quiver with Arrows Cernos Arsenal 2.png Cernos Arsenal 3.png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|sf740dQdrEA|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|Uub7Mjer8nk|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Cernos {{ver|25.7}} *Normalized quick shots to have the same critical chance/damage and status chance as charged shots. *While reviewing Bow stats the team has also refreshed all their FX (including the Lenz)! *Quick Shot increased from 110 to 190 *Charged Shot increased from 220 to 380 *Flight Speed increased from 85 to 90 *Aim Zoom decreased from 2.23x to 2x {{ver|25.0.7}} *Fixed the Cernos Energy color persisting as default on the strings. {{ver|22.12}} *Mastery Rank increased from 0 to 6. *Charged shot damage increased from 200 to 220. *Charge speed increased from 1s to 0.5s. *Status chance increased from 10% to 18%. *Critical chance increased from 35% to 36%. {{ver|11.1}} *Introduced. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Rakta Cernos}}, the [[Red Veil]] custom counterpart. *{{Weapon|Cernos Prime}}, the [[prime]]d counterpart. *{{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}, the [[Infested]] counterpart. *{{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}}, another Infested counterpart. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Cernos]] [[es:Cernos]] [[fr:Cernos]] [[Category:Bow]] [[Category:Tenno]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Update 11]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Impact Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Silent]] [[Category:Single-Shot]] [[uk:Цернос]]

{{Top|Orokin|Orokin|Orokin|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons|Prime|Prime|Prime|}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|A noble bow to hunt hellish beasts.}} The '''Cernos Prime''' is the [[Prime]] variant of the {{Weapon|Cernos}}. Aside from increased damage, the Cernos Prime is unique in that it fires three arrows per shot in a horizontal spread, and has an [[Alternate Fire]] mode that shoots vertically, and deals bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]]. It was released alongside {{WF|Valkyr Prime}} and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}}. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. *Deals '''50%''' bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]]. *Charged shots have innate 1 meter [[punch through]]. *Innate [[multishot]] of 3 arrows. **[[Alternate Fire]] can toggle a horizontal or vertical spread shot. *On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging enemies in their path and pinning the corpse to walls. *Can use the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. {{Advantages|class=Bow| *Fourth highest base damage of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Daikyu}} , {{Weapon|Lenz}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}}. *Pinpoint accuracy when aiming ({{Keybind|RMB}}). *[[Silent]]. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow| *Very wide spread. }} {{WeaponComparison|Cernos}} {{WeaponComparison|Rakta Cernos|header=n}} ==Acquisition== Unlike most Prime gear, Cernos Prime is permanently unvaulted, with relics being obtainable through [[Abandoned Derelict Caches]] in Corpus [[Railjack]] missions. {{PrimeTable}} {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ===Vaulted=== *On [https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1007828-limbo-prime-access-ending-soon-valkyr-prime-entering-the-vault/ September 11th, 2018], it was announced that Cernos Prime, along with {{WF|Valkyr Prime}} and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}}, would enter the [[Prime Vault]] and be retired from the reward tables on September 25th, 2018. Any preexisting components or fully-built weapons will remain as is. *Cernos Prime, {{WF|Valkyr Prime}}, and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}} can occasionally be acquired via [[Prime Resurgence]], in addition to having their relics obtainable as part of the aforementioned [[Railjack]] missions. ==Notes== *The +50% bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]] is multiplicative to other sources of +bonus damage on headshot such as {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}} and {{A|Prowl}}. *The Cernos Prime's shots fire multiple arrows in a fanning spread. The number of arrows is affected by [[multishot]] mods, similar to shotguns. *[[Alternate Fire]] toggles a Horizontal Spread or Vertical Spread fire. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}} will decrease accuracy by a small amount, making each arrow fire slightly off from its normal trajectory. **As of {{ver|19.11.2}} this was increased dramatically, making the weapon act more like a wildly-spreading shotgun than a fan of arrows. **The arrows seem to be spread in a formation where some arrows are lower than the others, rather than being wider spread than others, this might make it difficult to get headshots with multiple arrows. * Low accuracy will effectively invert Cernos Prime's firing mode. Horizontal shots will follow generally vertical line of shot and vice versa. This behavior is best observed while using [[Split Flights]] ==Trivia== *The Cernos Prime, alongside {{Weapon|Afuris Prime}}, {{Weapon|Akbolto Prime}}, {{Weapon|Aksomati Prime}}, {{Weapon|Akstiletto Prime}}, {{Weapon|Ballistica Prime}}, {{Weapon|Dual Kamas Prime}}, {{Weapon|Dual Keres Prime}}, {{Weapon|Fang Prime}}, {{Weapon|Gunsen Prime}}, {{Weapon|Paris Prime}} and {{Weapon|Zhuge Prime}} are the only Prime weapons that do not require [[Orokin Cell]]s as crafting ingredients. ==Media== TriBowCodex.png|Cernos Prime in Codex. Cernos Prime Arsenal.png|Cernos Prime as shown in the Arsenal Cernos Prime Arsenal 2.png Cernos Prime Arrow quiver.png|Cernos Prime Arrow Quiver with Arrows {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|wn1wlYu4yUk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|HCJ8hrCTUWE|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|7YPJ1kUyWIs|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Cernos Prime {{ver|30.9}} *Fixed the Cernos Prime Vertical Spread shot doing 2x damage of Horizontal Spread shot. {{ver|28}} *Reduced the hit FX of the Cernos Prime. {{ver|27.2.1}} *Increased Cernos Prime 10% Status Chance per projectile to 30% Status Chance per projectile. {{ver|27.2}} ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. {{ver|25.7}} *Normalized quick shots to have the same critical chance/damage and status chance as charged shots. *While reviewing Bow stats the team has also refreshed all their FX (including the Lenz)! '''Cestra Incarnon Genesis''' is an item that is used to add [[Incarnon]] upgrades to the {{Weapon|Cestra}}.

==Acquisition==
*Upon completion of [[The Duviri Paradox]] and [[Angels of the Zariman]], and unlocking [[The Steel Path]], players can earn {{Resource|Cestra Incarnon Genesis}} from [[The Circuit]]'s Steel Path to place on their Cestra with the help of [[Cavalero]] in the [[Chrysalith]]. This [[Incarnon Genesis]] form grants it evolutions to a transformation and newfound strength.
*Purchased from Cavalero for {{pc|120}}, complete with the resources used in its installation. This purchase can only be made '''once'''.

==Incarnon Genesis==
*Installing the Cestra Incarnon Genesis requires 20 {{Resource|Pathos Clamp|Pathos Clamps}}, 150 {{Resource|Saggen Pearl}}, and 80 {{Resource|Kovnik}}.
*When installed, the first Evolution tier is unlocked. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below;
**Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 [[affinity]] to the weapon, affected by [[Affinity Booster]]s.

====Overview====
*Weakpoint hits charge Incarnon Transmutation; Alt Fire transmutes. Switching back will expend any remaining charge.
*Mode switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's [[reload speed]].
*Incarnon Form is activated by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by achieving [[Enemy Body Parts|weakpoint hits]] and then pressing the [[Alternate Fire]] button. '''15''' weakpoints will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
**Charges '''do''' generate when hitting weak points highlighted by {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}}. 
***However, they do not generate from hits on {{A|Crystallize}}'s crystalline growths.
**Weakpoints on corpses or [[Invulnerable]] targets do '''not''' build charges.
**Individual [[Multishot]] bullets can build charges.
*Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Cestra's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing '''10''' rounds to a maximum of '''150'''. Once all ammunition is expended, the Cestra reverts to its normal form.
**Incarnon Form's magazine is '''not''' affected by mods.
**Incarnon Form is '''not''' affected by [[Ammo Efficiency]] (such as {{A|Energized Munitions}}).
**Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, [[bleedout]], or being [[disarm]]ed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon [[death]].
*Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.

'''Cedo Prime''' is the [[Prime]]d counterpart of the {{Weapon|Cedo}} alchemical shotgun, acting as a direct upgrade. Cedo Prime was released alongside {{WF|Lavos Prime}} and {{Weapon|Dual Zoren Prime}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Deals '''+60%''' bonus damage per unique status effect on target.
** On the Primary Fire, this bonus is '''additive''' to all base damage bonuses, such as [[Point Blank]] and [[Galvanized Savvy]].
** On '''direct hits''' from the Alternate Fire glaive, this bonus is additive with [[Galvanized Savvy]], and '''multiplicative''' to normal base damage bonuses like [[Point Blank]]. See [[Condition Overload (Mechanic)]] for more info.
** On '''explosions''' from the Alternate Fire glaive, this bonus does '''not''' apply.
*Primary Fire shoots wide-spread, close-ranged buckshot in a fully automatic fashion.
**Innate 0.8 meter [[punch through]].
**Innate [[multishot]] of 7 pellets.
*[[Alternate Fire]] launches a glaive that explodes in a '''6''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy and bounces up to '''11''' times.
**Direct hit and explosion apply status separately.
*** Direct hit deals {{D|Slash}} damage and has the listed status chance of '''50%''', affected by status chance bonuses and modded elements.
*** Explosion deals {{D|Blast}} damage and applies two separate '''guaranteed''' procs. The number of procs '''cannot''' be increased with status chance bonuses.
**** The first proc can be any element modded onto the weapon, or the innate {{D|Blast}} damage. The chance for each element follows normal status weighting rules.
**** The second proc has an even chance to be any of the following; {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, or {{D|Toxin}}.
**Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
**Consumes no ammo.
**[[Multishot]] affects the number of glaives released per use, each with their own trajectory.
*Innate {{M|Shotgun Ammo Mutation}} effect when used by Lavos.
*Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} and one {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarities.

{{Advantages|class=Shotgun|
*High magazine size.
*Alternate Fire:
**Tied with {{Weapon|Corinth Prime}}'s alt fire and {{Weapon|Trumna}}'s alt fire for the second highest status chance of all primary launchers, behind {{Weapon|1=Bubonico}}'s alt fire.
**No [[Damage Falloff]].
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Shotgun|
*Primary Fire:
**Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 3% from 26m to 52m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]).
*Alternate Fire:
**Glaive has travel time.
**Only one glaive (or set of glaives with multishot) can be active at a time, and takes approximately five<!--value needs testing--> seconds or 11 bounces to return.
**Will not launch glaive with 0 shotgun ammo. At least 1 round is needed, though it will not be consumed.
**Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]].
**Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions.
}}
{{WeaponComparison|Cedo}}
*Alternate Fire:
**Higher base critical chance (10.00% vs. 2.00%)
**Higher base critical multiplier (2.0x vs. 1.40x)
**Higher projectile speed (75m/s vs. 60m/s)

==Notes==
*The primary fire's bonus damage from individual status effects stacks additively with base damage mods and arcanes such as {{M|Point Blank}}, {{M|Blaze}}, {{Arcane|Primary Merciless}}, {{Arcane|Primary Dexterity}}, {{Arcane|Arcane Rage}}, {{Arcane|Arcane Primary Charger}}.
*Despite not consuming ammo when fired or to deal damage, the alt fire cannot be fired if the gun runs out of ammo.
*Tapping alternate fire once will return the glaive(s). Holding the alt fire or tapping multiple times does not reduce the return time.

==Tips==
*The [[Alternate Fire]]'s ability to rapidly proc multiple different status effects greatly synergizes with {{WF|Lavos}}'s {{A|Catalyze}}, its own primary fire, {{M|Galvanized Savvy}}, and melee weapons modded with {{M|Condition Overload}}.
*Despite the Primary Fire's low status chance, its high critical chance and critical damage multiplier make {{M|Hunter Munitions}} worth installing, which in turn allows for a free boost to the Primary Fire's damage even without any glaives launched.
*Installing [[Fatal Acceleration]] or [[Galvanized Acceleration]] or otherwise increasing [[Projectile Speed]] results in homing issues and faster glaive return, radically reducing the effectiveness of the [[Alternate Fire]].

==Trivia==
*The name ''Cedo'' may be from the Latin ''[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cedo#Latin cedo]'', which can mean "I cede, yield".

==Known Bugs==
* {{M|Galvanized Savvy}} and the innate '''60%''' effect are multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from alt-fire.
* Cedo Prime and its normal variant, {{Weapon|Cedo}}'s [[Alternate Fire]] stops exploding, bouncing correctly and applying random HECT status after a few minutes into the mission, if the player is not the host.

{{ver|38.0.12}}
*Reduced the speed of the Cedo Prime glaive from 105 m/s down to 75 m/s.
**We wanted to increase the flight speed of Cedo Prime's alt fire, enabling it to hit more enemies and return to the gun faster so that it could be fired more often. This made the auto-homing feature have a harder time steering to hit enemies, and despite giving it a sharper turning radius to compensate, it still tended to sometimes bounce out of large groups of enemies.
**The base Cedo glaive has a projectile speed of 60 m/s. Cedo Prime glaive had a speed of 105 m/s, and this hotfix brings it down to 75 m/s, hopefully striking a balance between the intention of more bounces quickly, and the ability to bounce multiple times the way a Cedo glaive is known to do!
*Fixed Cedo Prime's signature trait not applying to Lavos Prime.
*Fixed Cedo Prime's signature trait converting 100% of secondary ammo instead of the intended 50%.
